title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 — AgentKit, Agents API public beta, Decisions API, Bedrock managed agents, +20 updates
summary: OpenAI on September 29, 2026 at DevDay in San Francisco announced more than 20 major updates including AgentKit (production-grade agent toolkit), Agents API (public beta with hosted execution, memory, tools, multi-agent support), Decisions API (limited preview, uses Luna), Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents running OpenAI-powered agents inside AWS, Private Intelligence with ZDR + Private Safety Processing, and a $500 Pro subscription. Headline model: GPT-6.1 Sol (nearly matches GPT-6 Astra at 1/5 the price). Notably, GPT-6.1 Astra was scrapped — the Wall Street Journal reported cancellation over safety concerns (deception, agency without permission) flagged during internal testing.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol at DevDay — nearly matches GPT-6 Astra at 1/5 the price
summary: OpenAI on September 29, 2026 launched GPT-6.1 Sol at DevDay, a mere week after GPT-6 Sol. OpenAI says the new model delivers nearly the same level of intelligence as GPT-6 Astra for agentic coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth the standard input and output token prices. Available today in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users (not yet in Chat). Notably, GPT-6.1 Astra was scrapped over safety concerns — the Wall Street Journal reported OpenAI cancelled the release after researchers flagged higher deception and agency-without-permission behaviors during internal testing.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5 — 30% faster, 30% cheaper than Sonnet 5, $2/$10 per 1M
summary: Anthropic on September 28, 2026 released Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in the Claude 5.5 family and a faster, lower-cost complement to Claude Opus 5.5. Sonnet 5.5 runs 30%+ faster than Sonnet 5, costs up to 30% less for most work, and is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (unchanged from Sonnet 5) — but needs fewer tokens per task. Available on Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

title: NaiveAI releases Naive-N0.5-Flash — 309B/15.5B MoE built with AI-assisted research, 1M context
summary: NaiveAI on September 27, 2026 released Naive-N0.5-Flash, an open-weight 309B-total / 15.5B-active Mixture-of-Experts model with a native 1M-token context window and a custom inference runtime called NaiveRT (company-reported peak of 2,122 tokens/second on 8 GPUs in a single-stream test). The Beijing startup — associated with Tsinghua associate professor Jifeng Dai — describes the model as built by AI systems writing code, running experiments, monitoring results, and proposing iterations, with human researchers setting objectives and evaluation standards; starts from Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.5 base; combines sliding-window attention with DeepSeek Sparse Attention.

title: IFM open-weights K2-Horizon MoVA 36B/A4B — Apache 2.0, native 512K context, GPQA 80.8%
summary: The Institute of Foundation Models on September 29, 2026 released K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B on Hugging Face — a sparse mixture-of-experts checkpoint with 36B total / 4B active parameters, native 512K context, Mixture-of-Values attention design, and Apache 2.0 license. Published benchmarks: 80.8% on GPQA Diamond, 58.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 26.8% on Tau3-Banking; 19,390 downloads in first month.

title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K2.6 v2 — open-source multimodal agentic model with swarm orchestration
summary: Moonshot AI on September 24, 2026 released an updated Kimi K2.6, an open-source native multimodal agentic model focused on long-horizon coding, coding-driven design, proactive autonomous execution, and swarm-based task orchestration. The release ships on Kimi.com, the Kimi app, the Moonshot API, Kimi Code, and Hugging Face (modified MIT license); the API is OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible; inference engines vLLM, SGLang, and KTransformers are supported; launch partners include Fireworks AI and Cloudflare Workers AI.

title: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Action — 7B open-weight world action model for robot control
summary: Black Forest Labs on September 23, 2026 released FLUX 3 Action, an open-weight 7B world action model (WAM) derived from its multimodal FLUX 3 backbone and pretrained on video, image, and audio. The model takes a camera frame + text instruction and returns the next 2 seconds of actions, sets a new state of the art on RoboLab-120 at 38.3% success (±0.38) — beating Cosmos 3 Nano (36.8%) at less than half the parameters — and runs up to 3.95× faster on consumer GPUs in FP8. Weights ship under FLUX Kommunity License v1.0 with LeRobot integration.

title: China Telecom AI releases Xing4.0-29B-A4B — lightweight agentic LLM that runs on a single consumer GPU
summary: China Telecom AI on September 22, 2026 released Xing4.0-29B-A4B, a 29B-total / 4B-active MoE agentic LLM in the Xing series (formerly TeleChat). It is the first model of this scale trained entirely on the Ascend NPU platform with the MindSpore framework; natively supports 256K context (extensible to 512K); and is positioned for enterprise production deployments and local on-device runs on consumer GPUs. Compatible with vLLM, SGLang, and KTransformers; weights on Hugging Face.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5 — first in new Claude 5.5 family, 40% cheaper than Opus 5
summary: Anthropic on September 22, 2026 released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in its new Claude 5.5 family. It performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work, costs 40% less to run than Opus 5, was tested before release by external evaluators Frontier Design and METR, and scores strongest on Anthropic's automated behavioral alignment audit to date. Available via Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna — extends GPT-6 family to cost-efficient tiers
summary: OpenAI on September 22, 2026 released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, expanding the GPT-6 family beyond Astra. Both models use the same training methods as GPT-6 Astra and inherit its gains in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use, and alignment, but with higher usage limits and lower costs. Sol targets complex coding and agentic workflows; Luna is the cheaper tier; both are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for paid users, with Luna also accessible on free/Go tiers in the desktop app.

title: SpaceXAI/xAI releases Grok 4.7 — flagship for coding and knowledge work, same price as 4.6
summary: xAI on September 21, 2026 released Grok 4.7, its most capable model for coding and knowledge work. Per xAI the model works longer on difficult tasks, checks its own work more carefully, and ships with the best-calibrated safeguards to date; it is served at the same price and speed as Grok 4.6 and scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — tied with Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro (released the same day).

title: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo-V2.6-Pro — top open-weight model on AA Intelligence Index at 46
summary: Xiaomi on September 21, 2026 released and open-sourced MiMo-V2.6-Pro and MiMo-V2.6-Flash (both MIT-licensed), plus MiMo-V2.6-Pro-UltraSpeed serving at up to 20× the standard Pro output speed. Pro scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — tied with xAI's Grok 4.7 the same day — with 1.02T total / 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window; Flash is 309B/15B at $0.14/$0.28 per 1M tokens. Release includes weights, technical report, RL framework, and 7,000+ task environments.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Images 2.5 — Flare (default) and Sunburst (premium) API models
summary: OpenAI on September 8, 2026 released ChatGPT Images 2.5 with two API variants — GPT-Image-2.5 Flare (default, faster/cheaper) and GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst (premium, more capable). Both are rolling out in ChatGPT and the API as part of the company's continued investment in image generation quality and pricing tiers.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra — new flagship at $10/$50 per 1M tokens, SOTA on most benchmarks
summary: OpenAI on September 3, 2026 released GPT-6 Astra as its new flagship frontier model, priced at $10 input / $50 output per million tokens. Astra leads on most major benchmarks, including improved coding, math, and reasoning, and supersedes the GPT-5.6 Sol tier as the default top-tier model across ChatGPT and the API.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 — 75% cheaper cache reads, coding upgrades
summary: Anthropic on September 1, 2026 shipped Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, the latest rev of its flagship and largest models respectively. The release keeps $10/$50 pricing on the API but cuts cache reads by 75%, adds stronger coding and long-context performance, and introduces the Anthropic Model Hardware Standard (MHS) research preview for science workloads.

title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3 — better agent planning across email, calendar, and slide creation
summary: Meta on September 2, 2026 rolled out Muse Spark 1.3, the latest version of its Llama-based flagship. The update improves planning and execution across multi-step agent tasks — connecting to email and calendar, building slide decks, and completing tasks on behalf of the user across the Meta AI app and select WhatsApp surfaces.

title: Google ships Gemini 3.8 Flash — half the cost of 3.7 Flash, frontier-class latency
summary: Google on September 2, 2026 released Gemini 3.8 Flash as its new default Flash-tier model on the Gemini API and Vertex AI. Per Google, 3.8 Flash halves the cost per million tokens versus 3.7 Flash while improving latency, agentic tool use, and long-context retrieval; it is the recommended Flash model for production workloads going forward.

title: Anthropic unveils Model Hardware Standard (MHS) — research preview for science workloads
summary: Anthropic on August 27, 2026 released a research preview of its Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a specification aimed at standardizing how models expose capabilities for scientific computing — including FFI to native libraries, deterministic numerics, and structured data exchange. MHS is positioned as a counterpart to MCP for science workloads and is available in Claude.ai and the API for partner preview.

title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — cheaper inference with reasoning-quality retention
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team on August 26, 2026 released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a new Flash-tier entry in the Qwen3.8 family priced aggressively low at $0.15/$0.47 per million input/output tokens. The release is targeted at high-throughput batch inference while retaining reasoning quality comparable to the larger Qwen3.8 siblings, and is available via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and Hugging Face.

title: Google releases Lyria 3.5 — music generation model with longer structure and stem control
summary: Google DeepMind on August 26, 2026 released Lyria 3.5, the latest version of its music-generation model available via the Gemini API and AI Studio. Lyria 3.5 adds longer coherent musical structure, stem-by-stem control, and better vocal synthesis, and continues to power the MusicFX DJ and YouTube generative-music tools.

title: StepFun ships Step 5 Preview — 600B MoE with 27B active, 1M context, $1/$2.70 per 1M tokens
summary: StepFun on September 20, 2026 announced Step 5 Preview, a 600B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts flagship with 27B active parameters per token, a 1M-token context window, native image input, and AA Intelligence Index score of ~44. The API opens the same day at $1 input / $2.70 output per million tokens with a 95% cache discount; full open weights are scheduled for October 15, 2026.

title: InclusionAI releases Ling-3.0-flash-VL — 124B native multimodal MoE with image + video understanding
summary: InclusionAI on September 11, 2026 released Ling-3.0-flash-VL, a native multimodal extension of its Ling-3.0-flash MoE with 124B total / 5.5B active parameters, 1M-token context, and image + video input. It scores 42 on the AA Intelligence Index v4.1.1 (up 4 from the text-only base) and is priced on OpenRouter at $0.06/$0.18 per 1M input/output tokens.

title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash — 552B MoE with 16B-decode/8B-prefill, retires V4-Pro
summary: DeepSeek on September 10, 2026 released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, a multimodal MoE with 552B backbone parameters, native multimodal input, and a Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture that activates 16B parameters per token during decode but only 8B during prefill. Pricing is $0.30 input / $1.20 output per 1M tokens; V4-Pro retires to V4.1-Flash routing on September 14, 2026.

title: OpenBMB releases MiniCPM5-2B — 2.52B dense Llama-architecture on-device SOTA, Apache 2.0
summary: OpenBMB on September 7, 2026 released MiniCPM5-2B, a 2.52B-parameter dense Llama-architecture model with 131K native context, Apache 2.0 license, and an average score of 53.9 across 34 benchmarks (above Qwen3.5-4B at 51.1). Designed for on-device and resource-constrained deployment, it ships with BF16, GGUF, MLX, GPTQ, and DSpark draft variants; weights are available on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
